n: In 1836 Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Oliver Cowdery traveled to Salem, Massachusetts, partly hoping to find money to pay heavy Church debts. The Lord gently says he is not displeased, despite their “follies”—foolish choices.
The Lord points to a different kind of treasure: people in Salem who would later join the Church and strengthen Zion. Several years later, missionaries did baptize converts there.

f.g: Means or agency; acting as the Lord’s instrument.

n: They are to get to know people in the city, following the Spirit’s guidance.

The Lord promises that in time the city will be “given into their hands”—commonly understood as fulfilled through conversion and influence rather than wealth found on this trip. “Secret parts” likely refers to their private plans or vulnerabilities.

f.g: Probably hidden matters or weaknesses; the phrase echoes Isaiah 3:17. Its exact meaning here is uncertain.

n: The Lord tells them not to be anxious about their debts; he will give them ability to pay.

f.w: Concern not yourselves about your debts

n: Nor should they worry about Zion in Missouri; the Lord will be merciful to her.

f.w: I will deal mercifully with her

n: They are to stay in Salem and the surrounding area for a while.
The Lord will show them where to stay by the peace and power of his Spirit—a pattern for seeking guidance.

f.g: Made known by a sign; pointed out.

f.w: peace and power of my Spirit

n: They may rent lodging there. They are also to research the city’s early settlers and founders—some suggest this hints at family history, since Joseph’s ancestors lived nearby in Topsfield.

f.w: more ancient inhabitants and founders of this city
f.g: Salem was founded in 1626; Joseph Smith’s Smith ancestors had lived in nearby Topsfield.

n: There is “more than one” kind of treasure here—hinting that the most important riches are not money.
The Lord closes with Jesus’ advice to be wise as serpents yet without sin, and promises to arrange all things for their good as fast as they can handle it.

f.w: order all things for your good
